learning_outcomes.text: The student can name and explain the hygrothermal performance requirements of building components and their building physical background, and can frame these requirements within the growing sustainability goals of the construction sector.

The student can perform a performance analysis on concrete building and construction solutions for the building envelope (floor, facade, roof,...) and thus identify critical points and assess the value of building solutions available on the market. The student is also able to assess the maintenance possibilities, lifespan, and ecological impact (including reuse at end of life) of the solutions.
The student can apply the principles of a correct architectural solution for reading existing and designing their own connection details.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the principles of the performance approach in the light of general sustainability principles and within the challenges of climate disruption
Additional material knowledge: insulation materials, sealing materials, and air and vapor barriers
Performance-based study of the various building components:
Facades (re-insulation techniques, cavity wall, timber construction,...)
Roofs (pitched roofs, flat roofs, metal roofs)
Balconies, stairs, shafts, and interior finishing

Alongside the performance analysis of the various building components, current technologies and new developments are also discussed, with attention to sustainable solutions with minimal environmental impact.
Analyzing existing details (literature, manufacturer product sheets, site drawings,...)
Learning a methodology for designing details independently
